title: An import keeps only the site's own tables when the extension names its prefix, and reads several tables per request with db.dump_many when the site advertises it, producing the same SQL as db.dump
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/site/tracy-add-site/test/export-site-limits.test.mjs
S2: Read the exit code, the `# fail` line, and the `ok` line of every test named in run.tests.
expect: Prefix: with a prefix from db.tables only that prefix's tables are dumped (WordPress by base_prefix, multisite subsite tables kept); another install under a longer nested prefix is dropped only when its core tables exist, and a plugin table ending in options does not drop anything; with no prefix every table is dumped as before.

db.dump_many: used only when info advertises db_dump_many; batches respect max_tables; byte, time and error stops resume at next_cursor with no row repeated or missed; the SQL and the progress the customer sees equal the db.dump path for the same rows; without the capability the db.dump loop runs as before.
Failures: dump_failed is call_failed after one call on both paths; site 5xx is retried with the row limit halved; a stopped error repeated at the same cursor ends as call_failed instead of looping.
evidence: Before this change an import dumped every table in the database, other sites' included when a database holds several, and read each table with its own requests; a site with many small tables made many requests. This case pins the new behaviour with the tests below.
fence: The real export module against a fake engine that answers db.tables, db.dump and db.dump_many in the engine's documented shapes. Not shown: a real Joomla or WordPress database, a real multisite network.

tests: filters to a site prefix and uses db.dump_many progress and cursors when advertised
prefix filtering covers Joomla, WordPress single, multisite, nested sites, plugin tables, and legacy engines
db.dump_many honors max_tables, resumes byte/time budgets and a stopped error without repeating SQL
db.dump_many SQL and progress match db.dump for the same fake rows; missing capability falls back
db.dump_many dump_failed is a table error and is not retried
db.dump_many site 5xx retries and halves the row limit
legacy db.dump dump_failed is call_failed after one dump call
db.dump_many dump_failed is call_failed without retrying
stopped error resumes at its cursor and completes without repeating SQL
repeated stopped error at the same cursor ends after two calls
stopped error followed by first-page dump_failed ends as call_failed
a site that answers 500 above 1250 rows: the page halves until it fits, and the dump is whole
a site that answers 500 to every page, past every retry, is site_resource_limit
